nodes.description: Lifelong hemolytic anemia is the defining clinical feature; PKD is the most common red-cell glycolytic enzyme defect causing hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.

evidence.reference_title: Red cell pyruvate kinase deficiency: molecular and clinical aspects.
evidence.snippet: Red cell pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency is the most frequent enzyme abnormality of the glycolytic pathway causing hereditary non-spherocytic haemolytic anaemia.

nodes.description: Blockade at the terminal pyruvate kinase step causes accumulation of upstream glycolytic intermediates in erythrocytes, notably 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG / 2,3-DPG). Elevated intraerythrocytic 2,3-BPG shifts the hemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve rightward to enhance tissue oxygen offloading, partially compensating for anemia.

nodes.description: Because the mature erythrocyte lacks mitochondria and relies almost entirely on glycolysis for ATP, the block at the pyruvate kinase step impairs glycolytic ATP generation. Reduced ATP availability compromises cation-pump-dependent volume and membrane homeostasis, producing a metabolically damaged erythrocyte that is marked for premature removal.

evidence.reference_title: Red Blood Cell Metabolism in Pyruvate Kinase Deficient Patients.
evidence.snippet: Lacking a nucleus and organelles, red cells depend almost entirely on glycolysis for energy production.

evidence.reference_title: Red Blood Cell Metabolism in Pyruvate Kinase Deficient Patients.
evidence.snippet: Specifically, pyruvate kinase is responsible for catalyzing the ATP producing conversion of phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate, a process responsible for the generation of 50% of all ATP in RBCs

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function or missense variants in PKLR reduce the activity of the red-cell (R-type) pyruvate kinase isozyme, the enzyme catalyzing the final, ATP-generating step of glycolysis (phosphoenolpyruvate → pyruvate). PKLR is located on chromosome 1, and more than 150 different mutations in it have been associated with PK deficiency, giving a wide spectrum of residual enzyme activity that underlies the clinical heterogeneity. This is the disease-specific lesion that reduces erythrocyte metabolic integrity, the generic entry point of the conserved hemolytic-anemia module.

nodes.description: The metabolically damaged, ATP-depleted erythrocytes are prematurely cleared from the circulation, predominantly by macrophages of the spleen (extravascular hemolysis).
